statement: 'Most recently assessed' means the last matching fine in Library.Fines, which is oldest first (U5-D1). A fully paid but unwaived fine can still be waived; the waiver changes nothing about what was paid.

When a loan with an unknown notice is returned, that unknown notice is dropped. It no longer appears in unknown-notices, and confirm-notice for that copy reports 'no unknown notice'. No further notice can be sent for the ended loan, so nothing needs reconciling.
pay checks amount text first, then unknown member, then overpayment; a member owing nothing gets 'error: m1 owes only 0.00'; suspension does not block paying.

Holds.setAside picks the first hold in queue order with no copy set aside and an active member; deadline OpeningDays.pickupBy (return day + Policy.pickupDays 7, on or after); Holds.reservedFor replaces the head-of-queue check in Loans.borrow at the same position; for a copy not set aside, the first hold without a set-aside counts even if its member is suspended.

Ordering (Notices.historyOf): newest day sent first, then copy id ascending (ordinal string order, as in the L07 copy-id ordering). Two notices for the same copy on the same day can happen when a rejected notice is sent again that day; they are listed most recently sent first.

Each Fine gains `Paid: decimal` (0 to Amount). A payment only increases Paid, oldest fine first, and never changes Amount (DEC-006). No separate payment log is stored; R2 only asks for how much of each fine has been paid.

Hold gains SetAside: SetAside option (copy, until); None is waiting, so removing a hold frees its copy. On return the copy is set aside for the first waiting hold of a non-suspended member, until Opening.pickupDeadline (return day + Policy.pickupDays 7, on or after an open day); otherwise it is free. The JSON store writes an optional 'setAside' object per hold (missing = waiting); format stays 'lending/1'.
Policy.branchManagers (Tier 2) holds DEC-006 revision 2's names; an approver must match one exactly (case-sensitive); Waivers.BranchManager has a private constructor and is built only from that list.

Ordering: newest day sent first, then copy id. If one copy was notified twice on the same day (a resend after a rejection), the later notice is listed first. The title shown is the copy's book title (Views.titleOf).

LEND-L04-R3 is not implemented because Ordo reported ORDO.CONTRACT.UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT (CONFLICT-L04-STAFF-BORROWING); staff are treated like other members, so R2 (and L01-R2, DEC-005) still refuse staff borrows.
Help lists the three new commands directly after 'loans <member>' and before 'help'; README's command list is updated to match.

The pickup deadline is OpeningDays.dueDate(return day + Policy.pickupDays), with pickupDays = 7. It reuses the same open-day rule as due dates, so the rule exists in one place. Holds.setAside runs inside Loans.returnCopy after the loan is removed and any fine is assessed. Loans.Returned carries a Holds.Pickup option for the return text.
expire-holds removes SetAside holds whose deadline is before today and lists them by copy id. The freed copy is not passed on to the next member; it is a free copy under DEC-005/R2.
Fines.outstanding now sums the unpaid part (Amount - Paid), so `owes` (LEND-L04-R1) and the 5.00 borrowing threshold (LEND-L04-R2) use what is still unpaid without other changes.
JSON writes a root 'notices' array; a unit-7 store's per-loan 'notice' object is read as a log entry, so unknown notices stay unknown and are not resent.

The summary counts and outcome words are projected in Tier 3 (Views.ofNoticeRun), not counted in the CLI (ARC-HEU-03). `help` and the README command list gain the three commands after `waive <copy> <approver>`.

LEND-L08-R2 is not implemented because Ordo reported ORDO.CONTRACT.UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT (CONFLICT-L08-AUTOMATIC-RESEND) with accepted DEC-008; unknown notices are still never resent automatically, pinned by a test.
Loans made before revision 3 keep their stored due dates (no migration). Renewing such a loan adds the borrower's current period to the due date it has.
Existing holds of a member are left in place when they are suspended; suspension only blocks placing new holds.

OpenDays 2.0.0 made Calendar.nextOpen strictly-after; Policy.nextOpenDay now uses Calendar.onOrAfter so a due date already on an open day is kept (DEC-001/DEC-004 revision 2). Vendored files untouched.

Command flow: CommandLine.run 'waive' -> UseCases.waive -> Waivers.waive -> Views.ofWaiver (WaiverView). FineView gains WaivedBy, and 'fines' adds ', waived by <approver>' to waived fines only. Help lists 'waive <copy> <approver>' directly after 'fines <member>', and the README command list matches.
Library.Fines is already oldest first (Loans.returnCopy appends), so allocation and the fines listing use list order; the team-lead handoff saying newest first is false.
notices <member> reads the L07 notice log for that borrower, sorted by day sent (newest first) then copy id; same-copy same-day notices appear latest sent first.
Money owed is Fines.outstanding, the sum of every assessed fine; there are no waivers yet, so nothing is subtracted (DEC-006).

My unit 4 test expected a due date of 2026-05-03, a Sunday. Under revised DEC-001 the due date is now 2026-05-04, so the expectation was updated with a comment. This is a change mandated by the revised decision, not a regression.

Fines.outstanding did not leave out waived fines (no waiver existed); it now sums the unpaid part of fines that are not waived (Fines.counts), so owes, the LEND-L04-R2 borrowing restriction and the pay limit exclude waived fines, and Payments allocation skips waived fines.

Valid amounts are plain ASCII digits with an optional '.' and 1-2 decimals, greater than 0. Signs, exponents, thousands/comma separators, '.5' and '2.' are invalid, and so is a value too large for decimal. The Tier 1 type PaymentAmount (private constructor) carries the positive/two-decimal fact; Tier 3 parses the text.
Fine gains Paid: decimal (0..Amount); Amount never changes; Fines.outstanding (owes and the LEND-L04-R2 borrow check) sums Amount - Paid.

A payment is recorded as a new field on the fine, Fine.Paid (0 <= Paid <= Amount). Fine.Amount is never changed, as DEC-006 requires. No separate payments ledger (date or payer per payment) is kept, because R2 only asks for how much of each fine has been paid. Payments.pay is the only code that changes Paid.

The JSON store gains an optional `suspensions` array of { member, reason }, and the format tag stays 'lending/1'. A missing array decodes as no suspensions, so stores written by earlier versions still load. A store written now can still be read by older code, which ignores the extra array.

Command flow: 'pay' goes CommandLine.run -> UseCases.pay -> Payments.pay -> Views.ofPayment, and 'fines' goes UseCases.fines -> Views.memberFines. Help lists 'pay <member> <amount>' and then 'fines <member>' directly after 'owes <member>', and the README command list matches. An unknown member for 'fines' prints the existing 'unknown member' error.

Borrowing has a new reservation guard, in the same place in the guard order as before. A set-aside copy may go only to its member. Any other copy may go only to the head of the holds with no copy set aside (DEC-005), or to anyone when there are none. A suspended member at the head of the waiting holds still blocks free copies, as before L10. Copies freed by borrowing or expiry are not set aside again; they follow the free-copy rule ('simply free'). Renewal is unchanged: any hold on the book, set aside or waiting, still blocks renewal (LEND-L03).
A copy not set aside is lent only to the first hold with no copy set aside, read literally (a suspended member at its head is not skipped); the holds check stays after the loan-limit checks.

Setting aside skips only suspended members. Members who owe too much can still have a copy set aside (borrowing is then refused by LEND-L04-R2), and a copy set aside for a member who is suspended later stays set aside until it expires.
A set-aside copy is stored on the hold it serves (Hold.SetAside: { Copy; Until } option), so it cannot exist without a hold; removing the hold (borrowing, expiry) frees the copy.
Persistence: each fine gets an additive `waivedBy` field (approver name or null). Absent or null means not waived, so earlier stores load. The format tag stays `lending/1` (U1-D6).
Each delivery state is shown by its own label (delivered, rejected, unknown, confirmed delivered, confirmed not delivered), separate from the send-notices summary labels.

Existing tests changed by the new student/staff periods were updated. Due-date and amount checks get new expected values (BaseTests, L06WaiverTests, L10HoldPickupTests, L11ExportTests). The ordering tests (L02OverdueTests, L07NoticeTests) shift borrow dates so they keep checking ordering with the same due dates. The L09 sweep runs per member type.

LEND-L04-R3 is implemented only as far as no higher authority forbids: staff are exempt from the L04-R2 money-owed refusal (Policy.maxOwedToBorrow Staff = None). Staff borrows are still refused for an unknown member/copy, a copy already on loan, a suspension (LEND-L01-R2, owner Head of Lending) and a copy reserved for the head of a holds queue (DEC-005, accepted, owner Head of Lending). README says a requirement contradicting an accepted decision is not a revision of it, and Staff Services owns neither DEC-005 nor L01. So 'never refused for any other reason' does not hold, and R3 is reported not-implemented and escalated.

Notice state is stored on the loan itself (`Loan.Notice: OverdueNotice option`, holding the due date it was for, the day sent and a closed NoticeDelivery state). It disappears when the copy is returned, so a new loan of the same copy starts with no notice (LEND-L07-R3).

LEND-L08-R2 (automatically resend a notice once its delivery has been unknown for 2 days or more) is not implemented. It contradicts the accepted DEC-008 ('When we do not know whether a notice arrived, we must not send it again automatically'), owned by the Head of Lending. R2 was requested by Customer Services, and the README says a requirement that contradicts an accepted decision is not a revision of it. send-notices keeps the L07/DEC-008 behaviour, and a test pins it.

CLI: 'notices <member>' renders Views.NoticeHistoryView. An unknown member gives the existing UnknownMember error. Help lists the command directly after confirm-notice, and so does the README command list.

LEND-L04-R3 is not implemented because Ordo reports ORDO.CONTRACT.UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT (CONFLICT-L04-STAFF-BORROWING); staff are treated like every other member (including the LEND-L04-R2 refusal) until the owners resolve it.

OpenDays 2.0.0 changed Calendar.nextOpen to return the first open day after the given day (the old meaning is Calendar.onOrAfter). Opening now uses onOrAfter for due dates, the open command and pickup deadlines, so DEC-001/DEC-004 revision 2 hold again. The vendored file is not edited.

Hold gains SetAside: {Copy; Until} option; JSON adds optional per-hold 'setAside' (missing/null = none), format tag unchanged; removing a hold (borrow or expiry) frees its copy, which is not set aside again until its next return.

Fine gains Paid (0..Amount); Amount is never changed (DEC-006). Payments.pay fills the oldest fine first when the payment is made and also keeps a Payment (member, amount, day) in Library.Payments. Fines.outstanding (owes and the borrowing threshold) is the sum of Amount - Paid; this supersedes U4-D4's 'sum of all fines'.

Valid amount: plain invariant decimal (no sign/exponent/grouping), > 0, at most two written decimals ('2.500' refused), carried by Tier 1 PaymentAmount. pay checks amount, then member, then overpayment; paying when nothing is owed prints 'error: m1 owes only 0.00'.
What a member owes is the sum of all assessed fines via the existing Fines.outstanding (no exemption, no reduction; no payments or waivers exist yet).

'Oldest first' is the existing order of Library.Fines, which is assessment order (oldest first) because Loans.returnCopy appends each new fine. The team lead's handoff note (newest first) was not followed; see rejectedAssumptions.
In Loans.borrow the money-owed check runs right after the suspension check and before the copy lookup, loan limit and holds rules; the requirement does not dictate this order.
Hold gains State: HoldState = Waiting | SetAside of copy * until (Tier 1). A hold cannot be both waiting and holding a copy, and a set-aside copy always has a deadline.
Each Fine gains a Paid field; Amount never changes. What is owed (Fines.outstanding, used by owes and the L04 borrowing gate) is the sum of Amount - Paid.

LEND-L04-R3 was not implemented, and the R2 block applies to staff as to every member. Read literally, R3 ('a staff member's borrow is never refused for any other reason') contradicts the accepted decision DEC-005 (holds: copies go only to the head of the queue). README says a requirement that contradicts an accepted decision is not a revision of it, and Staff Services is not DEC-005's owner. R3 also contradicts LEND-L01-R2 (suspended members cannot borrow; owner Head of Lending) and LEND-L04-R2 (owner Head of Lending, no staff exemption). It cannot hold even in principle for an unknown copy or a copy already on loan. The part of R3 that is consistent, that staff may borrow up to their DEC-002 limit of 10, already holds through Policy.maxLoans. No exemption was added.

'owes <member>' is listed in help directly after 'overdue' and added to the README command list. No persisted state changed, because fines were already stored in the JSON 'fines' array. Money owed therefore survives a restart, and older stores load unchanged.

'Oldest first' means the order of the Library.Fines list. Loans.returnCopy appends each new fine to the end of that list, so the list is already in assessment order. It is not re-sorted by AssessedOn: the list order also settles fines assessed on the same day. The payment is spread across fines with List.mapFold when it is made, and each fine takes min(remaining, unpaid) before the next fine gets anything.

The opening-day rule is in a new Tier 2 module, Lending.Transition.OpeningDays. OpeningDays.dueDate moves a day to Calendar.nextOpen, and OpeningDays.check returns a closed alternative, Open | Closed of nextOpen. Both wrap the vendored OpenDays 1.4.0 calendar, which is not edited. VENDOR.md says OpenDays may be used from Tier 2.
Suspend/reinstate/member are added to the CLI usage list directly after 'loans <member>' and before 'help'. The README command list is updated to match.

One Tier 2 rule, Policy.dueDateAfter start = OpenDays.Calendar.nextOpen (start + 21 days), is used by both borrowing (start = borrow day) and renewal (start = current due date). This follows DEC-001 and DEC-004 revision 2.
The fines exemption for staff does not touch fine assessment: staff fines are still assessed and counted by `owes`, as DEC-006 (no member type exempt from fines) requires.

Contrary to the team lead's note, Fines.outstanding and Fines.pay did not exclude waived fines, so both were changed to skip them via a single predicate Fines.counts. `owes`, the LEND-L04-R2 borrowing check and payments all go through these two functions.

holds <book> lists the whole queue including suspended members; expire-holds removes only set-aside holds whose deadline is before today (waiting holds never expire), saves only when something expired, lines ordered by copy id.
The 5.00 threshold is Policy.maxOwedToBorrow in Tier 2; a member may borrow when owed <= 5.00 (Fines.ensureMayBorrow).
A payment's allocation is computed once when it is made (Fines.pay) and stored in Fine.Paid; fines assessed later start unpaid.
The store writes 'paid' on each fine and a 'payments' array; stores without them load with nothing paid and no payments; format tag stays lending/1.

Fine gains Paid (0..Amount); Fines.pay allocates oldest first and changes only Paid, never Amount (DEC-006); owed = sum of Amount - Paid, used by owes and the LEND-L04-R2 borrow block. JSON gains optional 'paid' per fine (missing = 0). No separate payment history is kept.

Borrowing applies the rule to borrowed day + 21. Each renewal applies it to current due date + 21, so a renewal counts from the already-moved due date, as DEC-004 revision 2 says ('21 days later than the current due date'). Loans already stored are not migrated: their due dates stay as recorded, even when one falls on a closed day.

Payments are applied to, and 'fines' lists, fines in Library.Fines list order, which is assessment order (oldest first): Loans.returnCopy appends each new fine and the JSON store keeps the order. The handoff note claiming newest first is false.

A loan counts as 'past its due date today' using the existing LEND-L02 overdue rule, Loans.overdue (days late > 0, so the day after the due date). A loan needs a notice unless its stored notice is for its current due date (Notices.needsNotice).
Unknown member is reported before already/not-suspended; a blank quoted reason prints 'error: a suspension needs a reason'; a missing reason prints the usage line.

Persistence: a top-level `notices` array replaces the per-loan `notice` object. Stores written by the L07 version are migrated on load: each loan's `notice` becomes a log entry for that loan. Earlier stores have neither field and load with no notices. The format tag stays `lending/1` (U1-D6).

I followed the requirement in skipping suspended members and members who already have a copy set aside when choosing whom to set a copy aside for. DEC-007 literally says 'the member at the head of the book's queue'. I treated L10 as a refinement of DEC-007, not a contradiction: L10 is owned by the same Head of Lending, says it implements DEC-007 revision 2, and a suspended member cannot collect (LEND-L01-R2). This is flagged in openQuestions.

To list every notice ever sent (including resends and notices for returned loans), notice state moved from Loan.Notice (U7-D1) into an append-only Library.Notices log of SentNotice. Each entry identifies its loan by copy, member and borrow date. The decision rules (needsNotice, unknown, confirm) use the latest entry for the current loan, so L07 behaviour is unchanged: unknown-notices and confirm-notice still consider only current loans.

Fines.ensureMayBorrow runs in Loans.borrow right after the suspension check and before the copy lookup and DEC-002/DEC-005 rules; threshold Policy.maxOwedToBorrow = 5.00, owing exactly 5.00 is allowed; holds and returns are unaffected.
Library.Fines list order is the assessment order, oldest first (returnCopy appends); payments and 'fines' use that order. The handoff claim 'newest first' was rejected.
Store: each hold gets an optional setAside object (copy, until); holds written earlier load with none. The format stays lending/1.

LEND-L08-R2 (automatically resend a notice whose delivery has been unknown for 2 days or more) was not implemented. It directly contradicts accepted DEC-008 ('When we do not know whether a notice arrived, we must not send it again automatically'), owned by the Head of Lending. L08 is only requested by Customer Services, and README says only the owner changes an accepted decision and a contradicting requirement is not a revision. The existing DEC-008 behaviour is kept and pinned by a test.

Durability: JsonCodec writes a top-level 'noticeHistory' array, and the format stays 'lending/1' (following U6-D6/U7-D6). A store without 'noticeHistory' (written before L08) starts its history from the notices kept on its active loans (historyFromLoans). Notices that were rejected, confirmed not delivered, or on loans already returned before L08 were never stored, so they cannot be recovered.

Each fine is stored with an optional 'waiver' object (approver, waivedOn) or null; missing means not waived; format stays 'lending/1'. help and README list 'waive <copy> <approver>' directly after 'fines <member>'; fines lines append ', waived by <approver>'.

holds lists Holds.queueFor in placement order via Views.bookHolds (unknown book reuses UnknownBook); expire-holds (Holds.expire) removes holds whose deadline is before today, orders them by copy id (ordinal) and saves; help and README list both directly after 'open <date>'.
Pickup deadline = Opening.onOrAfter(return day + Policy.pickupDays), with pickupDays = 7; the deadline day itself still counts.

waive targets the last unwaived fine for the copy in Library.Fines (oldest-first order, U5-D1), regardless of member or whether fully paid; refusal order: unknown copy, not a branch manager, no fine to waive.

The 5.00 threshold is the Tier 2 value Policy.maxOwedToBorrow, and the rule is Fines.ensureMayBorrow (owed <= 5.00 may borrow). It fails with a new LendingError case, MemberOwes(member, owed), rendered as 'member m1 owes 5.25'. In Loans.borrow it runs right after the LEND-L01 suspension guard and before the copy lookup and the DEC-002/DEC-005 checks. A suspended member who also owes therefore gets 'is suspended' (LEND-L01-R2: suspension is checked before every other rule), and a member who owes gets 'owes' even for an unknown copy. Holds, renewals and returns are not blocked, because R2 names only borrowing.
Copies are set aside only on return. A copy freed by expiry or by its member borrowing another copy is not set aside again; it follows DEC-005 (lent only to the first hold without a copy set aside).

JSON hold objects gain an optional "setAside" {copy, until}. When it is absent the hold is Waiting, so older lending/1 stores still load. `help` and README list `holds <book>` then `expire-holds` after `open <date>`.
No persistence change (the total is derived from stored fines). README's command list gains `owes <member>` after `overdue`.

Selection and ordering (days overdue descending, then copy id ordinal) live in Tier 2 Loans.overdue; Views.overdueLoans projects title and member name; CommandLine formats only (1 day / N days). 'overdue' with arguments prints 'usage: overdue' via the existing usage lookup.
LEND-L04-R3 is not implemented because Ordo reports ORDO.CONTRACT.UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT (CONFLICT-L04-STAFF-BORROWING) for it; staff borrowing keeps every existing rule.
JSON stores each fine's waiver as {approver, waivedOn} or null; a missing key loads as not waived; format tag unchanged.
Members are ordered with String.CompareOrdinal on the id (M1 < m1 < m10 < m2); an empty library exports only the header line.

On return, Holds.setAside picks the first Waiting hold of the book whose member is not suspended. The deadline is Policy.pickupDeadline = Calendar.onOrAfter (returned + 7 days). The return text gains ', set aside for X until D'.

The amount is validated before the member is looked up (`pay m9 x` prints the invalid-amount error), following the existing convention of addMember parsing its input first. Paying when nothing is owed prints `error: m1 owes only 0.00`. Suspended members may pay (LEND-L01-R2 restricts only borrow, hold and renew).
Check order in Fines.waive: unknown copy, then approver, then whether a fine is left to waive. The requirement does not give an order.

LEND-L08-R2 (automatic resend of notices unknown for 2+ days) is not implemented because Ordo reported an unresolved conflict with accepted DEC-008; DEC-008 behaviour is unchanged and pinned by a test.

notices <member> lists Notices.ofMember (Tier 2): day sent descending, then copy id ordinal, then the later of two notices for the same copy on the same day first; delivery names from Views.deliveryName; title from Views.titleOf; listed in help and README directly after confirm-notice.

What a member owes (Fines.outstanding) is now the sum of Amount - Paid over the member's fines. Both 'owes' (LEND-L04-R1) and the borrow block (Fines.ensureMayBorrow, LEND-L04-R2) use it, so paying a fine down to 5.00 or less lets the member borrow again.
`help` and README's command list gain `notices <member>` after `confirm-notice ...`.
'waive <copy> <approver>' is listed in help directly after 'fines <member>'; README updated.

Views.LoanView gains Renewed: int option (None when Renewals = 0). The Tier 3 projection decides whether a loan counts as renewed, so the CLI does no count comparison (ARC-HEU-03). It only appends ' (renewed N)' for Some N.

L12 agrees with the accepted decisions. DEC-001 revision 3 and DEC-004 revision 3 (Head of Lending) give the same periods (standard 21, student 14, staff 42) and the same renewal rule. No decision conflict exists.
Payments are also kept as a ledger (Library.Payments: payer, amount, date) in the order made, persisted in the store.
LEND-L04-R3 is not implemented because Ordo reported an unresolved conflict for it; staff borrows follow the same rules as other members, including LEND-L04-R2.
The JSON store gains an optional 'paid' on each fine (missing = 0) and an optional 'payments' array (member, amount, paidOn); format tag stays 'lending/1' because the change is additive, as in U1-D6.
Payments are also kept as a ledger (Library.Payments: member, amount, day); JSON adds optional 'payments' and per-fine 'paid' (missing = 0) with format tag unchanged.

Fine gains Waiver: Waiver option (approver, waivedOn). Waiving never changes Amount or Paid (nothing refunded). The waived fine is the last fine in Library.Fines (oldest first) for the copy that is not yet waived, whichever member it belongs to.
'overdue' is added to CLI usage directly after 'member <member>' and to the README command list. The 1 day / N days wording is presentation and lives in the CLI.

Amount syntax is digits with optional '.' and 1-2 digits, > 0 (PaymentAmount.parse, private constructor); '1.', '.5', signs, exponents, commas are invalid; checks run unknown member, invalid amount, then more than owed ('owes only 0.00' when nothing is owed).

OpenDays 2.0.0 changed Calendar.nextOpen to return the first open day strictly after the given day. The old behaviour (the given day when open) is now Calendar.onOrAfter. OpeningDays.dueDate and OpeningDays.check now call Calendar.onOrAfter, which brings back the DEC-001/DEC-004 revision 2 and LEND-L09 behaviour. The vendored file is not edited. On the merged HEAD, before this fix, 53 of 99 tests failed (due dates were moved off open days).

The history is a new Tier 1 list, Library.NoticeHistory : SentNotice list (oldest first), with SentNotice = { Copy; Member; DueDate; SentOn; Delivery: SentNoticeDelivery }. SentNoticeDelivery has five cases: SentDelivered, SentRejected, SentDeliveryUnknown, SentConfirmedDelivered and SentConfirmedNotDelivered. Loan.Notice (U7-D1) is still the only thing that decides whether a loan needs a notice. The history is a record of what was sent and does not drive resending. It outlives returns, so a returned loan's notices stay listed.
Notice text is built in Tier 2 from the book's title and the loan's due date (yyyy-MM-dd). Notices go to suspended members too, because L01-R2 restricts only borrowing, holds and renewals.
'pay <member> <amount>' and 'fines <member>' are listed in help, in that order, directly after 'owes <member>'; README command list updated.

Copy, member and borrow date identify a loan uniquely among loans that have notices: a loan gets a notice only once overdue, so it ended after its due date, and the next loan of that copy starts later.
Persistence: each fine in the JSON store gets an additive `paid` field. A fine without it (store from an earlier version) loads as paid 0. The format tag stays `lending/1` (as U1-D6).
'notices <member>' is listed in help directly after 'confirm-notice <copy> <delivered|not-delivered>'; README updated.

OpenDays 2.0.0 changed Calendar.nextOpen to 'strictly after the given day', which broke DEC-001/DEC-004 due dates (44 existing tests failed). Opening now uses Calendar.onOrAfter (the 1.x nextOpen) for due dates, pickup deadlines and the open command; the vendored file is not edited.
The most recently assessed fine is the last unwaived fine for the copy in Library.Fines (assessment order); a fully paid fine can still be waived.

Approvers are the closed Tier 1 type BranchManager = GraceHopper | AlanTuring (DEC-006 revision 2), matched by exact name; a waiver is Fine.WaivedBy: BranchManager option, leaving Amount and Paid unchanged. JSON gains optional 'waivedBy' (missing/null = not waived).

UseCases.parseDate (Tier 3 input translation) accepts exactly ASCII digits yyyy-MM-dd forming a real day; anything else, including 2026-02-30 and surrounding spaces, is the new LendingError.InvalidDate printed 'error: invalid date 'x' (yyyy-MM-dd)'. Opening.ofDay (Tier 2) gives Open or Closed(day, nextOpen); Views.ofOpeningDay projects it; 'open' with a wrong word count prints 'usage: open <date>'; help and README list 'open <date>' directly after 'notices <member>'.
The branch managers are Policy.branchManagers (Grace Hopper, Alan Turing) from DEC-006 revision 2, matched exactly.
'owes <member>' is listed in help directly after 'overdue'; README command list updated.
History is newest first by day sent, then copy id, later send first for the same copy and day; outcomes print as delivered, rejected, unknown, confirmed delivered, confirmed not delivered.
`help` and README's command list gain `waive <copy> <approver>` after `fines <member>`. `fines` appends `, waived by <approver>` to waived fines.
Waived fines are excluded from Fines.outstanding (owes, LEND-L04-R2 borrow block) and from payment allocation in Fines.pay; they remain listed by 'fines' with their approver and paid amount.
The '2' in `(renewal N of 2)` is taken from Policy.renewLimit through Views.RenewView, not written in the CLI.

confirm-notice: the answer is parsed first (as in U5-D5), into a closed Notices.StaffAnswer. A non-existent copy prints `error: unknown copy c9`, as other copy commands do; a copy not on loan or without an unknown notice prints `error: no unknown notice for c1`.

LEND-L08-R2 (automatic resend of unknown notices after 2 days) is not implemented because Ordo reports ORDO.CONTRACT.UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT (CONFLICT-L08-AUTOMATIC-RESEND) with accepted DEC-008; send-notices keeps DEC-008 behaviour.
Durability: JsonCodec writes 'waivedBy' only on waived fines. A fine without it, including every store written before L06, loads as not waived. The format stays 'lending/1'.

A valid amount matches digits with an optional point and one or two digits and is above 0 (signs, exponents, commas, '2.' and '.5' are invalid); Payments.parseAmount (Tier 2) is the only way to build a PaymentAmount. Refusal order: invalid amount, unknown member, payment above owed ('error: m1 owes only N.NN', including 0.00). Suspended members may pay.
open <date> requires an exact yyyy-MM-dd calendar date (invariant culture, TryParseExact) and answers from Policy.isOpen / Policy.nextOpenDay.

What a member owes is the existing Fines.outstanding: the sum of all fines assessed under the schedule. Nothing pays or waives fines yet; DEC-006 waivers, when added, must be excluded from this sum. Store format unchanged.
waive refusal order: unknown copy, then approver not a branch manager, then no fine to waive. Fines of suspended members may be waived.

Fines.isOwed (Waiver = None) is the single rule for whether a fine counts. Fines.outstanding filters on it, so 'owes', the LEND-L04-R2 borrow block and the pay-over-owed check all leave out waived fines. Payments.apply skips waived fines, so a payment never goes onto one. The part of a waived fine that was already paid stays in Paid, and nothing is refunded.

The 5.00 threshold lives in Policy.maxOwedToBorrow (Tier 2), citing LEND-L04-R2 because no docs/decisions record covers it; the check is `owed <= 5.00`, so exactly 5.00 may borrow. A refused borrow prints `error: member m1 owes <amount>` with the full amount owed.
'owes <member>' is listed in help and README directly after 'overdue'; the amount is formatted with the existing two-decimal Views.money.
In Loans.borrow the owed check runs after the member lookup and suspension check and before the copy, loan-limit and hold rules.
A suspension records its reason and the date it was imposed (SuspendedOn, via the Clock port); only the reason is displayed.
pay/fines output uses Views.money and Views.date; help and README list 'pay <member> <amount>' then 'fines <member>' directly after 'owes <member>'.

The rows are projected in a new Tier 3 module, MemberExport. Views.fs is already at 390 lines, near the size limit. Each row reuses Views.memberTypeName and Views.money. Status comes from Standing.suspensionOf, and owes from Fines.outstanding, the same function `owes` uses. Rows are sorted with String.CompareOrdinal on the member id.
A suspended borrower's 'renew' prints 'error: member m1 is suspended' before any DEC-004 reason, keeping LEND-L01-R2 (suspension checked before every other lending rule).

A copy set aside is part of the hold. Tier 1 Hold has a new field, SetAside: SetAside option, where SetAside = { Copy; Until }. None means the member is still waiting. So a set-aside copy always belongs to exactly one hold and has exactly one deadline, and removing the hold (on borrowing or expiry) frees the copy without any extra step. In JSON, 'setAside' is written only when present. Holds stored before L10 have no 'setAside' and load as waiting.
Fines.unpaid returns 0 for a waived fine; outstanding (owes), the LEND-L04-R2 borrowing gate and Fines.pay all use it, so waived fines are excluded everywhere what is owed is computed.
expire-holds removes holds whose deadline is strictly before today and lists them by copy id; holds with no copy set aside never expire.
Owing more than 5.00 affects only borrowing; holds, renewals and returns are unchanged.
The store writes an optional 'waiver' object per fine; fines without it load unwaived; format tag stays lending/1.
overdue is read-only and lists every overdue loan regardless of the member's standing (suspended members included).
In Loans.borrow the money-owed check comes after the DEC-002 loan-limit check and before the DEC-005 holds check. The requirement does not give an order (only suspension is required to come first).
A waiver is recorded on the fine (Fine.Waiver: approver and date); Amount and Paid are unchanged, nothing is refunded, and a waiver is never removed.

What a member owes is the existing Tier 2 function Fines.outstanding, the sum of every assessed fine of that member. Nothing is subtracted, because DEC-006 lets only a named approver's waiver reduce a fine and waivers do not exist in the system yet. 'owes' goes CommandLine.run -> UseCases.owes -> Views.owed (Views.OwedView). Amounts use Views.money, so they always have two decimals. An unknown member gives the existing UnknownMember error.
The unit-4 test expecting a Sunday due date (2026-05-03) now expects 2026-05-04 under DEC-001 revision 2; only the expected date changed.

The approvers are Policy.branchManagers = {Grace Hopper, Alan Turing}, taken from DEC-006 revision 2. Names are matched exactly (case- and space-sensitive). A stored waiver keeps its approver's name even if the list is later revised, because it is a record of what happened.

A waiver is recorded on the fine as `Waiver: Waiver option` with the approver's name (DEC-006: 'recorded with the approver's name'). Amount and Paid are untouched, so nothing is refunded. No waiver date is stored, because none is asked for.

Library.NoticeHistory (append-only SentNotice list with five outcomes) records every notice, alongside Loan.Notice which still drives sending; both are updated only in Notices.sending/record/confirm. Entries link to a loan by copy + borrowed-on day; history outlives loans; pre-L08 stores load with an empty history (no reconstruction). Order: day sent descending, copy id, later notice first.
The 5.00 threshold (Policy.maxOwedToBorrow, Tier 2) applies to every member type including staff; owing exactly 5.00 is allowed; refusal prints 'error: member m1 owes N.NN'.
Borrowing checks keep their order: the hold rule (Holds.ensureMayLend) stays where the DEC-005 check was. Renewal is unchanged: any hold on the book refuses it (DEC-004).

Notice state moves from Loan.Notice into Library.Notices (a log in send order: copy, member, borrowedOn, dueDate, sentOn, outcome); a loan's current notice is the latest entry with its copy and borrow day; L07 commands behave as before.
Oldest first is the order of Library.Fines, which is assessment order because Loans.returnCopy appends new fines; the handoff claiming newest-first order was not relied on.
Durability: JsonCodec writes a 'paid' value for each fine. A fine stored without 'paid' (written before L05) loads with Paid = 0. The store format stays 'lending/1'.

OpenDays 2.0.0 made Calendar.nextOpen strictly after the given day (old behaviour renamed Calendar.onOrAfter); OpeningDays.nextOpen now calls Calendar.onOrAfter so due dates and pickup deadlines move only when the library is closed. The vendored file is unchanged.
expire-holds removes holds whose deadline is before today and does not set the freed copy aside again; waiting holds never expire.

Fine gains Waiver: Waiver option (Approver, WaivedOn); Fines.unpaid is 0 for a waived fine, so Fines.outstanding (owes, LEND-L04-R2 borrow check, LEND-L05 overpayment check) and the LEND-L05-R2 allocation leave it out; Paid and Amount are kept, nothing refunded.

The DEC-006 revision 2 branch managers are Policy.branchManagers. Names must match exactly (ordinal, case-sensitive, no trimming), so 'grace hopper' is rejected. Waivers.Approver has a private constructor, and only Approver.approver creates one after checking the policy list. Waivers.waive is the only code that sets Fine.Waiver.

A valid amount must match ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?$ and be greater than 0. Signs, exponents, commas, a leading '.' and a trailing '.' are rejected with the new LendingError InvalidAmount ('invalid amount 'x''). The check lives in Tier 2 as Payments.PaymentAmount, whose constructor is private, so only parse can create one. The new error PaymentExceedsOwed renders as 'm1 owes only 1.50'. Checks run in this order: unknown member, then invalid amount, then payment over what is owed. Paying more than is owed, including when the member owes 0.00, records nothing.

A waiver is recorded on the fine as Fine.Waiver : Waiver option, where Waiver = { Approver: string } (Tier 1). Amount and Paid are unchanged by a waiver. No waiver date is kept, because neither DEC-006 nor L06 asks for one. The approver is stored as a plain name so that a waiver stays valid history if a later DEC-006 revision changes the list of managers.

Holds.ensureMayLend replaces the DEC-005 head-of-queue check in Loans.borrow at the same place in the refusal order: a set-aside copy only to its member, any other copy only to the first waiting hold. A copy freed by expiry, by its member borrowing another copy, or because the only waiting member is suspended is not set aside again; it follows the waiting queue.

The 'of 2' in the renew message comes from Policy.renewLimit through Views.RenewView.Limit, and the renewal number is the loan's Renewals count after renewing. Neither number is written in Tier 3 or Tier 4.
waive checks unknown copy first, then the approver, then whether a fine is left to waive.

Policy.branchManagers holds the DEC-006 revision 2 names, matched exactly; checks run unknown copy, not a branch manager, then no unwaived fine; the last unwaived fine for the copy in assessment order is waived, whichever member owes it.

`renew <copy>` calls the existing Tier 2 rule Loans.renew unchanged; refusal reasons and their order (overdue, limit, holds) come from it and the existing error texts in Views.describeError, so DEC-004 stays the single authority.

Two L04OwesTests expectations encoded due dates on Sundays (2026-05-03; 2026-04-19 inside the fine sum), contradicting DEC-001 revision 2 (2026-03-01); they now expect the next open day (due 2026-05-04; owes 2.00 instead of 2.25). What they check is unchanged.
Policy.maxOwedToBorrow = 5.00 (refuse when owed > 5.00); in borrow the check runs after the suspension check and before copy lookup, loan limit and holds.

Borrow checks Holds.reservedFor: a set-aside copy is reserved for its member. Otherwise the copy is reserved for the first Waiting hold of the book (DEC-005). That member may be suspended, so a suspended head of the queue still blocks free copies, which is a literal reading of R2. Borrowing removes the borrower's hold on the book; any copy set aside for them becomes free.
README's command list and `help` gain `pay <member> <amount>` and `fines <member>` after `owes <member>`.

LEND-L08-R2 is not implemented because Ordo reports ORDO.CONTRACT.UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT (CONFLICT-L08-AUTOMATIC-RESEND); DEC-008 stays in force: an unknown notice is never resent automatically, pinned by a test.

Notices.recordSent appends one history entry for every notice sent, including rejected ones. Notices.confirm also updates the matching unknown entry (same copy, member, due date and day sent) to confirmed delivered or confirmed not delivered. The title is looked up from the copy's book when the history is shown, not stored.

'expire-holds' removes only holds that have a copy set aside with Until < today. A waiting hold has no deadline and never expires. The output is sorted by copy id using ordinal string order on the id. 'holds <book>' lists the whole queue in placement order, set-aside holds keep their position. Help and the README list 'holds <book>' and 'expire-holds' directly after 'open <date>'.
periods lists the member types in DEC-001's table order (Policy.memberTypes), using the type names the member command shows.

Suspensions are held in Library.Suspensions (Map<MemberId, SuspensionReason>) rather than on Member; standing is derived by Library.standingOf as the closed type Standing = Active | Suspended of SuspensionReason; SuspensionReason has a private constructor refusing blank text.

PaymentAmount is a Tier 1 type with a private constructor (tryCreate: > 0, at most two decimals); amount text must be digits with an optional '.' and one or two decimals; signs, exponents, separators, '.5' and '2.' are invalid.
A blank suspension reason is refused with 'error: a suspension needs a reason', after the unknown-member and already-suspended checks.

The team lead's note and build-reports/opendays-2.0.0.md say OpenDays 2.0.0 passed CI with no code changes needed. That is false: 2.0.0 changed Calendar.nextOpen to mean strictly after the given day (Vendor/CHANGELOG.md), and 30 tests failed. Policy.dueDateAfter and Opening.status now use Calendar.onOrAfter, which keeps the DEC-001/DEC-007 meaning. The vendored file is unedited. Committed separately as 0c5e2a4.

Tier 2 Loans.overdue computes days overdue with Fines.daysLate (the function returnCopy uses), keeps loans with days > 0 (so a loan due today is not overdue) and sorts by days descending then copy id (ordinal).

A set-aside copy is stored on its hold (Hold.SetAside: copy and deadline); removing the hold frees it. Deadline = next open day on or after return day + 7. Store stays lending/1 with optional setAside; older stores load holds as waiting.
`help` and README's command list gain `open <date>` after `notices <member>`. No persistence change.

Existing tests with student/staff loans that assumed 21 days were updated only where revision 3 changes what they check: due dates in BaseTests and L10HoldPickupTests, the student fine in L06WaiverTests (3.75), the notice body in L07NoticeTests (due 2026-03-16); L02OverdueTests' ordering test now lends all three copies to standard member m1 so it still checks the copy-id tiebreak and '1 day'.
What a member owes is Fines.outstanding, the sum of all assessed fines; DEC-006 waivers are not implemented, so no fine is excluded.
`owes <member>` totals all of the member's recorded fines with the existing Fines.outstanding (no waivers exist yet, so nothing is subtracted); amounts are rendered with Views.money (two decimals).

'Most recently assessed' means the last matching fine in Library.Fines, which is kept oldest first (appended). The fine must be for the copy, of any member, and not yet waived. Checks run in this order: unknown copy, then not a branch manager, then no fine to waive. The new LendingErrors are NotBranchManager and NoFineToWaive.
